# The US Government Is Under AI Cyberattack

By Thomas Brewster,

Forbes Staff.

 Senior writer at Forbes covering cybercrime, privacy and surveillance.

Nov 25, 2026, 12:59pm EST

The CIA is among a number of American agencies being targeted in attacks with links to a Chinese-made AI tool. (Pool Photo by David Burnett/Newsmakers)

Getty Images

Hackers have targeted a number of U.S. government and intelligence departments, according to reports this week, which suggest the attacks are being fuelled by AI.

Among the targets are the CIA, the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency and the Office of the Director of National Intelligence, according to the New York Times. The cyberattack doesn't appear overly serious, affecting unclassified reconnaissance data. 

However, per the Times, the attackers used a tool called Artex, which combines open source AI models to test network and computer defences. It was released by a Chinese coder earlier this year, but they've since removed the tool from their Github account, after Artex was used in myriad attacks, including one on the European Union.

Earlier this year, the FBI warned about the widespread use of Artex by cybercriminals and spies alike. 

Shaun Williams, senior director for customer intelligence at SentinelOne, says that "the widespread availability of AI-powered tools like Artex have allowed threat actors to find and exploit vulnerabilities in internet facing devices faster, more effectively, cheaper, and with less skill than ever before."

Earlier this year, Forbes reported on an AI-generated cyberattack using a similar tool to Artex, which saw the hackers get access to hundreds of thousands of credit card details.

(Photo by Nikolas Kokovlis/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

NurPhoto via Getty Images

U.S. officials suspect Iran of cyberattacks on as many as 50 ships carrying oil and other explosive substances, the Wall Street Journal reports.

Signal is taking a stand against AI agents, blocking assistants built into iPhones and Android devices from accessing chats. It's also warning that such agents present a threat to user privacy, calling on tech giants like Apple, Google, and Microsoft "to provide simple technical tools and accurate documentation that give developers like Signal ways to prevent AI agents from accessing sensitive application data."

## Winner of the Week

Crowdstrike announced it is acquiring another cybersecurity giant, Zscaler, for $43.9 billion. George Kurtz, CEO of Crowdstrike, said the merger could create "the largest AI safety and security company the world has ever seen."

## Loser of the Week

FinCen, the U.S. Treasury's financial intelligence unit, says it has also been targeted by hackers, reporting an "incident that resulted in unauthorized access to a limited subset of its systems." It is not, however, providing any information on what precise data is affected or how the attack happened.
